title: Honi and the Carob Tree
text:
The Talmud tells that Honi the Circle Maker was troubled by a verse in the Psalms about the return from exile: "We were like dreamers." Seventy years of exile, he wondered; can a person really dream for seventy years?

One day, walking along the road, he saw a man planting a carob tree. Honi asked him how long it would take for the tree to bear fruit. "Seventy years," the man said. Honi asked whether he really expected to live seventy years to eat from it.

The man answered that he had found the world full of carob trees. His ancestors had planted them for him, and he was planting this one for his own children.

Honi sat down to eat his bread, and sleep came over him. A rock formed around him, hiding him from sight, and he slept for seventy years. When he woke, he saw a man gathering fruit from the carob tree. He asked whether he was the one who had planted it. "I am his grandson," the man said.

Honi went home and to the study house, but no one believed he was Honi, and no one treated him with the respect he was used to. Grieving, he prayed for death, and died.
lesson: Much of what we enjoy was planted by people who never saw it bear fruit. Do something today for grandchildren you may never meet.
people: Honi the Circle Maker, an old man planting
